## 1. Overview

`bibliolatam` is an R package designed to bridge Latin American and Iberian diamond open-access literature into mainstream bibliometric pipelines (`bibliometrix` and `biblioshiny`).

While major commercial bibliometric indexes (such as Web of Science and Scopus) under-represent regional scholarship, platforms like **SciELO**, **Redalyc**, **BDTD** (theses and dissertations), **Oasisbr**, and **LA Referencia** host millions of peer-reviewed articles and research outputs. `bibliolatam` provides robust parsers, author normalization engines, and API clients to adapt these heterogeneous outputs into canonical `bibliometrixDB` objects.

---

## 2. Author Name Normalization

Latin American author naming patterns frequently include generational suffixes (*Junior*, *Filho*, *Neto*, *Sobrinho*) and compound particles (*da*, *de*, *do*, *del*, *van*). Traditional parsers often split these incorrectly.

`normalize_authors()` standardizes names into the canonical `SOBRENOME INICIAIS` format while preserving suffixes:

```{r setup}
library(bibliolatam)

# Single author with suffix and particle
normalize_authors("Jose da Silva Junior")

# Multiple authors separated by semicolons
normalize_authors("Batista Filho, Jose Rodrigues; Perez Gomez, Maria del Carmen")

# Vector of author strings
authors_vec <- c("Gama, Gabriel", "Antonio Carlos Neto", "Maria das Gracas Souza")
normalize_authors(authors_vec)
```

---

## 3. Parsing Local Files

`bibliolatam` includes dedicated offline parsers with automated delimiter and encoding detection:

- `read_scielo()`: Tabular CSV/TSV exports from SciELO.
- `read_scielo_jats()`: Full-text NLM/JATS XML articles, reconstructing cited references (`CR`).
- `read_spell()`: Administration and accounting exports from SPELL / ANPAD.
- `read_bdtd()` / `read_oasisbr()`: Brazilian theses, dissertations, and institutional repository records.
- `read_redalyc()`: BibTeX, RIS, or CSV exports from Redalyc / AmeliCA.

Example reading a bundled sample:

```{r parsing}
sample_scielo <- system.file("extdata", "scielo_sample.csv", package = "bibliolatam")
if (nzchar(sample_scielo)) {
  df <- read_scielo(sample_scielo, convert = TRUE)
  head(df[, c("AU", "TI", "SO", "PY", "DB")])
}
```

---

## 4. The `bibliometrixDB` Data Contract

All converters enforce the `bibliometrixDB` class contract via `as_bibliometrix()`, ensuring full compatibility with `bibliometrix::biblioAnalysis()`:

```{r convert}
raw_df <- data.frame(
  AU = c("SILVA J; SANTOS M", "GAMA G"),
  TI = c("Science in Latin America", "Open Access Ecosystems"),
  SO = c("Revista de Saude Publica", "Ciencia da Informacao"),
  PY = c(2022, 2023),
  DI = c("10.1590/test1", "10.1590/test2"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

bdf <- as_bibliometrix(raw_df, dbsource = "scielo")
class(bdf)
head(bdf$SR)
```

---

## 5. Merging & Deduplication

When combining records from multiple regional platforms (e.g. SciELO and Oasisbr), `merge_bibliolatam()` resolves entities using DOI matching and Levenshtein title distance:

```{r merge}
df1 <- as_bibliometrix(raw_df[1, , drop = FALSE], dbsource = "scielo")
df2 <- as_bibliometrix(raw_df[1, , drop = FALSE], dbsource = "oasisbr")

merged <- merge_bibliolatam(df1, df2, match_by = c("doi", "title"), verbose = FALSE)
nrow(merged)
```

---

## 6. Standalone Interactive Application

`bibliolatam` provides a complete standalone Shiny web interface integrating all search, download, parsing, and merging capabilities:

```r
if (interactive()) {
  bibliolatam::run_app()
}
```
